title: Module 13 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: The null hypothesis for a test of a Pearson correlation is
o: The population correlation rho equals zero
items.why: It states there is no linear relationship in the population.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for testing a Pearson correlation are
items.why: Two means are estimated, one for each variable.

items.q: A correlation is statistically significant when
o: The absolute value of r exceeds the critical value for the df
items.why: Critical values of r depend on df and alpha, and shrink as n grows.

items.q: With n = 30, the critical r at alpha = .05 two-tailed is about
items.why: With df = 28 the critical r is .361. An obtained r of .41 would be significant.

items.q: The Spearman correlation is used when
o: The data are ranks or the relationship is monotonic but not linear
items.why: It applies Pearson's formula to ranks.

o: A dichotomous variable to a numeric variable
items.why: For example, gender (coded 0 and 1) and a test score.

o: A nominal variable with three levels and a numeric variable
items.why: It is Pearson r computed on two variables coded 0 and 1.

o: Whether a measure assesses what it claims to
items.why: A reliable scale gives similar results under the same conditions.

o: Whether a measure assesses what it is intended to measure
The consistency of scores over time
items.why: A measure can be reliable without being valid, but it cannot be valid without being reliable.
It reflects how strongly the items on a scale correlate with one another.
